description: We are a team of creative and curious sixth-grade girls from Austin who are excited to explore space, science, technology, and engineering. We enjoy working together, sharing imaginative ideas, solving problems, and learning new skills. This is our first NASA Space Apps Challenge, and our goal is to have fun while creating an innovative and meaningful project.
summary:
Mars Madness is a physical board game with a companion app that challenges players to survive a 30-day mission on Mars. We developed a decorated game board, 3D-printed astronaut pieces, and printable and digital challenge cards inspired by NASA Space Place.

Players work individually or in teams, roll a virtual die, move their astronauts, and enter a card number into the app. Each card presents a space survival problem, and players’ decisions affect resources such as oxygen, water, food, power, health, and safety. The app tracks these changes. If any status drops below zero, the team loses; otherwise, the first team to finish wins.

We combined ideas from familiar board games, tested several designs, and improved the rules and balance. We used an MIT App Inventor prototype for inspiration, Claude to help develop the app, and ChatGPT to help create the cards.

Our project addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning space exploration into hands-on learning. It helps young explorers practice teamwork, problem-solving, and resource management while understanding why everyday decisions matter during a Mars mission.
details:
Mars Madness combines a physical board game with a companion app to help players learn how to survive a 30-day mission on Mars.

How it works
One or two teams, with up to three players each, roll a virtual die, move their 3D-printed astronauts, and draw challenge cards. Players enter the card number into the app and choose how to respond. Their decisions affect six elements: oxygen, water, food, power, health, and safety. If any status drops below zero, the team loses. The first team to finish while surviving wins.

Research and learning
Each team member researched one or more of the six elements: why astronauts need them, how they obtain or maintain them, and what happens when resources run out or conditions become unsafe. We also explored NASA’s simulated Mars missions in Houston. This research shaped our challenge cards, while the resource points were designed for balanced gameplay.

Tools and creativity
We made a decorated board, 3D-printed astronaut pieces, and printable and digital cards. NASA Space Place informed our scenarios. An MIT App Inventor prototype inspired the app’s design, Claude helped develop the app, and ChatGPT helped create the cards.

Inspired by Candy Land, Chutes and Ladders, and Sorry!, we tested several designs and improved the rules through team discussions and voting. Our game addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by making space survival an opportunity to practice teamwork, problem-solving, and resource management.
